label: prf:unit-modulus-eigenvalue
title: Proof of unit modulus eigenvalue
html:
Proof. The Hecke relation \sigma_i^2 = h\sigma_i + 1 (where h = q - q^{-1}) gives each generator eigenvalues q and -q^{-1} on V_{(2,1)}, with product q \cdot (-q^{-1}) = -1. For a product of n generators, \det\bigl(\rho_{(2,1)}(\beta)\bigr) = (-1)^n. When n is even, \det = 1, so the eigenvalues satisfy \lambda_1\lambda_2 = 1. Combined with |\mathrm{tr}| \le 2 (which holds for real traces of 2 \times 2 matrices with unit determinant), both eigenvalues lie on the unit circle.

For the Borromean braid (n = 6 generators): \det = 1 and the Lean-proved closed form (thm:borromean-markov-trace-closed-form) together with the Wedderburn decomposition yield \chi_{(2,1)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) = -2. The characteristic polynomial is then \lambda^2 + 2\lambda + 1 = (\lambda + 1)^2 = 0, giving the degenerate eigenvalue \lambda = -1. \square

Eigenvalue table

Operator (3) V_{(2,1)} eigenvalues (1^3)
\sigma_i q q,\; -q^{-1} (real) -q^{-1}
L_+ = \sigma_1\sigma_2 q^2 e^{\pm i\theta_L}, \lvert\lambda\rvert = 1 q^{-2}
\mathfrak{M}_+ (meson) q^6 e^{\pm i\theta_M}, \lvert\lambda\rvert = 1 q^{-6}
\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} (proton) 1 -1 (degenerate) 1

At q = q_0: the Hopf link has phase \theta_L \approx 59°; the meson braid has \theta_M \approx 54°; the Borromean braid has \theta = 180° (the unique fixed point on the unit circle where \lambda = -1).

The baryon--meson duality

The sign of the (2,1) contribution to the Markov trace distinguishes the two sectors:

  • Baryons (\theta = \pi, \cos\pi = -1): the standard representation contributes negatively. This is the structural origin of the factor \dim V_{(2,1)} = 2 appearing as a multiplier in the proton substrate identity — the (2,1) channel is subtracted from the symmetric channel.

  • Mesons (\theta \approx 54°, \cos\theta > 0): the standard representation contributes positively. All-positive-crossing braids force the symmetric eigenvalue q to dominate, but the (2,1) channel adds rather than subtracts.

The unit-modulus constraint means the (2,1) channel carries phase information (the angle \theta) but no amplitude growth — only the (3) and (1^3) channels exhibit geometric growth (q^n and q^{-n}). Mass ratios between different braids therefore arise from the interplay of real geometric growth on the outer channels and oscillatory phase rotation on the standard representation.
